Options:
A m,n are parallel lines
B m,n are skew lines
C m,n are coplanar lines
D m,n are non-intersecting lines
Given two lines lying in two parallel planes. They can be parallel (if directions same) or skew? Let's examine: If alpha // beta distinct parallel planes. Line m in alpha, n in beta. They cannot intersect because planes disjoint (assuming parallel distinct; in Chinese 平面α//平面β usually means parallel, may be distinct, not same). Any point on m is in alpha, any point on n in beta. If they intersect, point belongs to both planes, impossible. Thus they do not intersect. In 3D, non-intersecting lines can be parallel or skew. Always true: they are non-intersecting lines (不相交直线). Are they necessarily not parallel? No. A not always. B not always (can be parallel). C not always? If parallel, two parallel lines are coplanar (any two parallel lines determine a plane). If skew, not coplanar. So C not always. D always. Need final line 答案：D.

由于平面 \(\alpha \parallel \beta\)，且 \(m\subset \alpha\)，\(n\subset \beta\)，所以直线 \(m\) 和 \(n\) 不可能相交；它们可能平行，也可能异面，因此一定正确的是“不相交直线”。
